notes:
I couldn't do this research. My first attempt to fetch the source pages failed with the message "no more code_execution tool calls remaining this turn," and a second try was blocked the same way. Because of that, I didn't read any pages from the approved sites. That includes enduringword.com, biblehub.com, studylight.org, preceptaustin.org, netbible.org and the others.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any notes on Song of Solomon 5:1–16. Anything I wrote now would come from memory and couldn't be checked against a page, which is exactly what you asked me not to do.

**Once my tools are available again (for example, in a new message), this is the plan:**

1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:**
   - Enduring Word's Song of Solomon 5 page
   - The Bible Hub pages for 5:1 to 5:16, which include Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Matthew Henry and Barnes
   - StudyLight's commentary pages
   - Precept Austin
2. **Where traditions differ:**
   - Wesley's Explanatory Notes (wesley.nnu.edu)
   - Spurgeon's sermons on this chapter (spurgeon.org), such as those on v. 2 (the beloved knocking) and v. 16 ("altogether lovely")
   - Desiring God and GTY on how to read the Song: as a picture of Christ and the church, or literally as human marriage
   - Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition and Monergism for the Reformed view
   - 1517.org and lcms.org for the Lutheran view
   - Seedbed and Pentecostal/charismatic sites (pneumareview.com, ag.org) where they have something
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible translator notes (for example on the dew in v. 2, the latch in v. 4 and the beating in v. 7)
   - Bible Odyssey on the Song's genre and love poetry
   - Catholic and Orthodox readings on newadvent.org, catholic.com and oca.org, such as Church Fathers and mystical readings of the soul and the Bridegroom
   - Popular modern teaching only if the sites actually discuss it

If you resend the request or just say "try again," I'll carry out this plan and write the notes verse by verse ("v. 4: …"), with a URL after every point and anything I can't find left out.
